{"redo_desc_about": "Our 3 day SurfGroms program caters to groms between the ages of 5-12 years old. Become a Surfer for Life with the SurfGrom Program! SurfGroms is a fun-filled, learn-to-surf program that teaches kids the essentials of ocean awareness and safe surfing. {"redo_desc_about": "#Intimate guided walk through Puketi Forest, the ancient kauri rainforest (15,000 hectares) close to the Bay Islands. Listen and maybe see the native birds: tui, fantail, pied tit, fernbird and kukupa. Spot the Northland green gecko and tusked weta. Experienced guides with a passion for conservation share their stories and knowledge: Learn more about the unique flora and fauna. {"redo_desc_about": "All aboard for a pleasant evening's journey from Mt Barker to Strathalbyn while celebrating Christmas in July with a difference. The journey commences from Mount Barker station - a pleasant 20 minute drive from Adelaide along the South Eastern Freeway. Your ticket includes a twilight three-course dinner at a Strathalbyn hotel and return travel from Mt Barker. Leaving Mt Barker late afternoon, listen to our heritage steam locomotive, as it hauls the train up to the crest of the line at Philcox Hill and then winds down the eastern escarpment of the southern Mt Lofty Ranges, passing through several long abandoned station sites which bear testimony to the importance of this branch line a century ago. Crossing the Angas River you then enter the historic township of Strathalbyn where many Scottish migrants settled in the early 1800s, influencing the early architecture which is still evident today. {"redo_desc_about": "Sparsely populated - save for the wildlife who call this rugged coastline home - the Catlins in the southern tip of the South Island offers views of some of New Zealand’s most stunning natural beauty. Your tour begins at 8am from your accommodation as we head south along the Southern Scenic route, through the sea-side village of Brighton before stopping for photos at the mouth of the mighty Taieri River. Continuing on you will go through Waihola and Balclutha before arriving in Owaka, the gateway to the Catlins. Your first short walk takes you to Nugget Point, the most iconic landform of the Otago Coastline. From here you will see the several rugged rocks likened to gold nuggets where NZ fur seals and many NZ seabirds can be viewed. If you visit between December and February there is always the chance of seeing a huge Elephant Seal from the viewing platform. Continuing south our next stop is at a picturesque bay known to be a favourite haul-out site for the rarest sea lion in the world, the New Zealand sea lion. After being hunted to near extinction, only about 200 remain on the mainland. Stand in awe of their magnificence, you’ll be as close as 10 metres from one of these wonderful marine mammals. Driving through native coastal rainforest surrounded by ancient trees your next short walk takes you to the highest waterfall in the Catlins. Your guide will introduce you to several native bush birds and native plants before you arrive at the McLean Falls, arguably the most spectacular of all the waterfalls in the Catlins. Further south you will get the opportunity to look for one of the rarest and smallest dolphins in the world – the Hectors dolphin. The nutrient-rich waters attract this dolphin to become resident in one of the bays on the Catlins coast during the warmer months. You will be taken to the best vantage points to look for these dolphins while your guide prepares light refreshments. Your last stop is at a 180 million year old petrified forest that is revealed at low tide. The fossilised remains of an ancient forest can clearly be seen, representing one of only three accessible sites in the world. Depending on your travel arrangements, our guide can drop you off when the tour ends at 6pm in Invercargill, the Stewart Island Ferry Terminal or take you back to your accommodation in Dunedin.", "redo_desc_highlights": "", "redo_desc_what_included": "Tour includes guide, vehicle and Department of Conservation fees only.", "redo_desc_what_excluded": "Lunch is not included however we’ll make a stop in the township of Owaka where there are several options.", "redo_desc_itinerary": "Departure Time- 7:30am inside Port Chalmers or from all centrally located accommodation. Return Time- 5:30pm.", "redo_desc_what_to_bring": "On fine days shorts or light trousers and everyday shirts are fine however we advise that you come prepared in case there is a ‘Southerly Change’. To do this, wear three layers on top and bring a waterproof jacket. Wear shorts or light trousers (avoid denim and cotton) and good footwear. {"redo_desc_about": "We take you to see the Governor Generals' residence from the lake and present a well researched commentary on some of the early European history of the area. Visit Old St Paul’s Cathedral (optional, entry $5 NZD per person).", "redo_desc_itinerary": "**09:30-10:00 AM – Tour pickups**

**10:00-10:30 AM - Mt Victoria Lookout**
Begin your day with a scenic drive along the picturesque Wellington Waterfront and Oriental Bay, admiring the elegant seaside homes and the quirky private cable cars that scale Wellington’s steep hillsides, before ascending to Mt Victoria Lookout, where panoramic 360-degree views showcase the city, harbour, and surrounding hills — a perfect introduction to New Zealand’s capital.

**10:50 AM – “Blown Away” Sign Photo Stop**
Pause for a quick photo opportunity at Wellington’s iconic “Blown Away” sign, a playful nod to the city’s famously breezy weather.

**11:00-11:15 AM – Visit the Weta Cave, Miramar**
Continue to Miramar for a visit to the world-renowned Weta Cave Shop — the public gateway to Weta Workshop. Discover the magic of movie-making with a short documentary, explore the mini museum, and take photos with incredible life-sized sculptures from films like The Lord of the Rings and Avatar.
(Note: This stop includes time to browse the shop and museum but does not include a Weta Workshop tour.)

**11:30-12:15 PM – Seaside Lunch Stop**
Savour a relaxing lunch (mains and a drink included) at one of Wellington’s charming seaside cafés or restaurants, soaking up coastal views and local atmosphere.

**12:30 PM – Wahine Memorial Park & South Coast Exploration**
After lunch, visit the Wahine Memorial Park, commemorating one of New Zealand’s most tragic maritime disasters. Continue your journey along Wellington’s rugged South Coast, exploring the Taputeranga Marine Reserve and Te Kopahou Reserve Visitors Centre — where wild coastline and sweeping views meet fascinating natural history.

**1:30-2:00 PM – Brooklyn Wind Turbine Lookout**
Travel inland to the Brooklyn Wind Turbine, one of Wellington’s landmarks, offering spectacular panoramic views over the city and harbour.

**2:15-2:45 PM – Wellington Cable Car & Botanical Gardens**
Return to the city for a chance to experience the Wellington Cable Car (optional, ticket not included). Stroll through the beautifully landscaped Botanic Gardens, finishing at the Lady Norwood Rose Gardens, home to more than 100 rose varieties in bloom during summer.

**2:45-3:00 PM – Parliament Buildings & Old St Paul’s Cathedral**
Drive by (or, time permitting, walk through) the Parliament precinct, including the famous Beehive. If time allows, visit Old St Paul’s Cathedral (optional, entry $5 NZD per person) — a stunning example of Gothic Revival architecture built entirely from native timbers and adorned with exquisite stained-glass windows.

{"redo_desc_about": "Visit one of New Zealand’s Geothermal wonders situated in the Whakarewarewa on a half day tour from Auckland City. Te Puia Geothermal Valley Rotorua is an active geothermal wonderland! Tour starts with us picking you up from Auckland CBD; then you enjoy a three-hour scenic drive towards the Bay of Plenty. On arrival, you will be welcomed by the Māori residents and offered to choose your steam box meal (extra cost) to be cooked in Woven baskets and placed in the active steam vent. After that; your tour guide will take you through a 60 mins tour around 60 hectares of Te Puia Geothermal Valley including the largest active geyser in the Southern Hemisphere, the Pohutu Geyser. You can also See the native Kiwi bird, Mud Pools, watch New Zealand’s iconic native Carvings and Weaving performed in front of you, as well as Learning about the Māori Culture while performing at the sacred Marae. {"redo_desc_about": "Experience the very best of Auckland city as well as the Waitakere Ranges on Auckland’s famous West Coast on a small group in one spectacular day. Enjoy this full day tour with TIME Unlimited Tours, winner of multiple global awards including the National Geographic World Legacy award. Enjoy an amazing full day experience including lunch with the very best overview of Auckland City and its glorious West Coast. Marvel at views of several ancient volcanoes on the Auckland isthmus. Travel through the Auckland Domain with the Auckland Museum as its centrepiece, stopping to enjoy views of Auckland’s 2nd-largest volcano. Continue through the boutique suburb of Parnell, restored in the old colonial style and with many beautiful mansions. Explore Tamaki Drive, one of the world’s most beautiful city drives, along Auckland’s waterfront, looking out at several of the stunning beaches along Auckland's shoreline. See Mission Bay, arguably Auckland’s most well-known beach with lovely golden sand. Enjoy great views of the famous Hauraki Gulf and the mystical island volcano Rangitoto Island, Auckland’s largest and youngest volcano at 600 years old. Drive over the iconic Auckland Harbour Bridge, spanning the sparkling blue waters of the Waitemata Harbour dotted with white sails, from which you can marvel at the iconic view back to Auckland’s skyline. Visit the Arataki Visitor Centre at the gateway to Te Wao Nui o Tiriwa, the great forest of the Maori ancestor Tiriwa, also known as the Waitakere Ranges. Witness spectacular ocean vistas of both the Manukau Harbour and along Auckland’s wild West Coast. Get up close to some of New Zealand’s unique indigenous flora and fauna. View soaring cliffs, roaring surf and spectacular volcanic black sand beaches. {"redo_desc_about": "Join us for a unique and exclusive Wellington sightseeing experience. Shenandoah, one of our favourite Wellington tours and exclusive to Xplor Tours, takes you to perhaps the best but least known destination in the region. Approximately 20 minutes’ drive from Wellington, overlooking the sparkling Pauatahanui Inlet and linked with Battle Hill (a significant Maori War site), Shenandoah is a working farm and hidden historical gem inside a native wild birdlife reserve. Once Xplor Tours drops you there, owner and proud Kiwi Simon takes you on a unique and magical tour around his beautiful, relaxing property, and through its history. Originally a Maori Fortress Pa for Ngati Toa in the 1800’s, the property has seen three different owners over 150 years. After withstanding a major battle with English troops, it became a Crown Fort to guard the stagecoach road from highway robbers. Some of the first settlers to New Zealand made contact with the local iwi here, before the whalers and settlers transformed Pauatahanui into the thriving rural community of today. Early in World War II, Shenandoah was commandeered as a US Marine training base and housed over 100,000 troops, ushering in the next military episode of the site. The history isn’t just told in stories though; behind the barn doors, a private museum is filled with artifacts found on the property which date back over the last 150 years. As part of your day trip to Shenandoah with Xplor Tours, you can relax by the pond and jetty or other seating areas in the gardens, and enjoy a tea or coffee with morning or afternoon tea. Simon’s passion and ability to enthral makes this Wellington tour experience genuinely unique and one that will stay with you long after you leave Shenandoah. {"redo_desc_about": "Welcome to the world’s largest classroom, covering more than 1.3 million square kilometers (over half-a-million square miles). Listen to a presentation from our local guide about the evolution of the School of the Air. Learn how technology have changed the delivery of education in Outback Australia and how our Outback families integrate their children’s educational needs with the challenges of remote living. Watch a short film which provides a snapshot into the lives of our students and their tutors, as well as seeing what it is like for our teachers to visit our Outback families. Our broadcasting studio presentation is the most popular experience in our Visitor Centre! Learn about our children's history, dreams, and aspirations by browsing through samples of the children’s work in their many varied forms on display. {"redo_desc_about": "An alpine pass, and a pristine mountain lake. All within easy reach of Christchurch. What more could you ask for? At a little over 930m this is a highest point on SH 73, which links Canterbury to the West Coast, even higher than the better know Arthurs Pass! An added bonus is Lake Lyndon on the other side of the pass.", "redo_desc_highlights": "", "redo_desc_what_included": "- Pickup from some of the main hotels within Christchurch, or alternately from the Canterbury Museum
- Expert, knowledgeable guide
- Photography tuition (if required)
- Late model, air conditioned transport
- Snacks, beverages, and drinks
- Scenic stops", "redo_desc_what_excluded": "", "redo_desc_itinerary": "Join us as we head west out of Christchurch straight for the Southern Alps foothills via the scenic Canterbury Plains before we make a first stop at Aylesbury Corner to take advantage of the scenic lookout platform. If we’re there at the right time we may even get to see one of the massive coal trains that are coming and going from the West Coast.
From here we continue along the West Coast Rd via Sheffield and Springfield to our next stop where we stretch our legs once more and enjoy the mountainous vistas opening up in front of us before resuming our westward journey into the foothills, taking on the increasingly steep climb up Porters Pass followed by a dizzying descent down the other side to Lake Lyndon where we stop for a drink and nibbles while enjoying the scenery and fresh air.
From Lake Lyndon we make our way another 4 km north-west along the West Coast Rd to a lookout point above dry stream with amazing views out over the Porter River and Whitewater Stream towards Castle Hill with Broken Hill and Mt Manson adding to the scene. This is the turn around point for us, but not the end of the tour as we’ve plenty more amazing things to take as we retrace our steps to Christchurch, beginning with Porters Pass itself.
From Porters Pass we gaze upon and admire the alpine views surrounding us; West is Mount Enys and the Craigieburn Range, East is the West Coast road snaking its way down the hill towards the Canterbury Plains, just visible over the tops of the hills ahead of you. Either side of us is Foggy Peak to the north and the slopes of the Kowai Forest and Big Ben range to the south.
Heading back towards Christchurch we detour across the Waimakariri Gorge Bridge for a last stop but one (time permitting) admiring the historic bridge and the river gorge it crosses before continuing along South Eyre Rd to the North Canterbury town of Kaiapoi for that final picturesque stop on the banks of the Waimakariri River Regional Park, before winding up our trip back in the city.", "redo_desc_what_to_bring": "", "redo_desc_duration_text": "4.5 Hours (Half Day Tour)", "redo_desc_requirements": "", "redo_desc_cancellation": "", "redo_desc_check_in": "", "redo_min_age": "", "redo_max_age": "", "redo_group_size": "", "redo_meeting_point": "", "redo_desc_other": ""}

Queenstown to Milford Sound and Te Anau: Early start as we head to Milford Sound with numerous stops to enjoy and photograph the scenery before arriving in Milford Sound for a scenic cruise on the fiord. More stops to explore the environment on our way back out to Te Anau

{"redo_desc_about": "This fantastic Eco tour begins at your hotel and the historical Rocks area of old Sydney. Heading westwards across the coastal plain we make our way to the Great Dividing Range of Australia. Our first stop today is Featherdale; this unique park gives visitors the opportunity to discover over three hundred different varieties of unique Australian wildlife. Reboarding the vehicle we continue west towards the Blue Mountains National Park. We enter a little known hidden clearing to enjoy some home style morning tea. You will have time to roam the area and seek out the wild kangaroos and birdlife that frequents this part of the National Park. Next we visit some scenic lookouts to view the Blue Mountains such as King’s Tableland, Eagle Hawk and Narrow Neck lookout, enjoy the stunning sights of the three sisters as you overlook the magnificent Jamison Valley. Lunch today is at the charming village of Leura. Here you will have a chance to stroll the main street before settling down at the delightful Leura Garage Cafe. Enjoy fresh and healthy local produce in the funky surrounds of a converted garage. After lunch we skirt around cliff drive towards the township of Katoomba. At Eagle Hawk lookout you will see the famous 3 sisters Rock formation and marvel at the stunning views of the Jamieson Valley. From here we continue around Narrowneck Plateau for more incredible vantage points. This afternoon we travel to the scenic Evan’s Lookout for more gorgeous views of the Blue Mountains and finish the day with a visit to Scenic World and the famous Scenic Rail, a four hundred and fifteen meter decent through the cliff side tunnel will take you into the ancient rainforest itself. {"redo_desc_about": "Explore Tropical North Queensland’s natural treasures with us.

Pressed for time???

Join our Cairns Explorer Tour where the reef meets the rain forest, and immerse yourself in the stunning contrasts of the beautiful ancient World Heritage rainforest.

Escape the ordinary and immerse yourself in the lush beauty of Tropical North Queensland on this flexible half-day adventure. Designed for nature lovers and thrill-seekers alike, this tour combines rainforest walks, crystal-clear swimming holes, and iconic sights—all packed into one unforgettable experience.

Your journey begins with a guided walk through the Cairns Botanic Gardens, where you’ll uncover the fascinating story of the region’s ancient rainforest and its unique evolution. Relax and take in breathtaking views as you travel along scenic tropical roads surrounded by stunning landscapes.

Pause at the secluded Crystal Cascades, a peaceful rainforest gem, before heading to Behana Gorge, where you’ll take a refreshing dip beneath the spectacular Clamshell Falls. {"redo_desc_about": "Departing Sydney at 0600 and only 90 minutes from Sydney, the Central coast has some beautiful habitats and bird species not found so easily in Sydney. Ourimbah Rest Stop is a great place to start. We look for Bassian Thrush, Regent Bowerbird, Green Catbird, Yellow-throated Scrubwren and other rainforest species. We then head off to Central Coast Wetlands (Pioneer Dairy) where over 230 species have been recorded, including a variety of waterbirds and Red-rumped Parrots. Tuggerah Wetlands is close by and has a variety of waterbirds as is McPherson Road Swamp, where we may see the giant Black-necked Stork. Palmdale is an exciting stop for Australian Logrunner, Noisy Pitta, Rose Robin and White-headed Pigeon. Final stop is St Huberts Island to locate the elusive Bush Stone-curlew. Expect to identify 80+ species. {"redo_desc_about": "Welcome to our Beginner Drone Photography Workshop, a comprehensive course designed specifically for those interested in exploring the exciting world of aerial photography. This workshop is perfect for those who have recently purchased their first drone or who are looking to upgrade their photography skills to include aerial perspectives.

The course starts with introducing the fundamentals of drone operation and safety guidelines to ensure you fly responsibly and within legal boundaries. We then delve into the technicalities of drone photography, such as understanding and adjusting drone camera settings, mastering flight modes, and learning about various drone models and their capabilities.

Our workshop further explores the creative aspects of drone photography. You will learn about composition techniques from an aerial perspective, such as leading lines, patterns, and symmetry. We will also cover different lighting conditions, teaching you how to work with natural light and use it to your advantage to create stunning aerial shots.

Throughout the course, you will have hands-on practice sessions under the supervision of our experienced instructors. These sessions will provide you with real-world experience, helping you apply what you have learned, refine your skills, and build confidence in drone operation and aerial photography. {"redo_desc_about": "Riding a trick skateboard is an exhilarating experience that combines balance, agility, and creativity. Designed specifically for performing tricks, these skateboards feature smaller, harder wheels and narrower decks compared to cruisers or longboards. These characteristics make trick skateboards ideal for technical manoeuvres like ollies, flips, grinds, and aerial tricks, especially in skate parks and urban environments.

The first step in mastering a trick skateboard is building a solid foundation in balance and control. Learning how to properly stand on the deck, control your speed, and steer using your body weight are essential skills. Once comfortable, riders can begin practising basic tricks like the ollie, which is the foundation of many more advanced tricks. An ollie allows skaters to lift the board off the ground without using their hands and is crucial for jumps and aerial stunts.

As riders progress, they can experiment with more advanced tricks like kickflips, where the skateboard rotates underfoot while airborne, or grinding on rails and ledges. Each trick requires precise foot placement and timing, demanding hours of practice to perfect. Skating on smooth surfaces like concrete in skate parks or streets is ideal for these types of tricks, as hard wheels give better speed and control on such surfaces.

In addition to technique, riding a trick skateboard also emphasises creativity and personal style. Skaters often combine tricks, develop their own variations, and find unique spots in urban landscapes to showcase their skills. The individuality of skating is a big part of its appeal, making it more than just a sport, but a form of self-expression.

Overall, riding a trick skateboard requires patience, practice, and persistence, but the rewards are immense. It’s a challenging, dynamic sport that continually pushes your limits, offering an ever-evolving sense of accomplishment and fun.", "redo_desc_highlights": "", "redo_desc_what_included": "", "redo_desc_what_excluded": "Helmets and Pads are available to hire separately.", "redo_desc_itinerary": "", "redo_desc_what_to_bring": "", "redo_desc_duration_text": "Multiple Hire Times", "redo_desc_requirements": "", "redo_desc_cancellation": "", "redo_desc_check_in": "", "redo_min_age": "", "redo_max_age": "", "redo_group_size": "", "redo_meeting_point": "Shop 2, 49 North Steyne Street, Manly NSW 2095", "redo_desc_other": "A waiver will also need to be signed prior to hire."}

{"redo_desc_about": "Giiyong | Welcome - to Thaua Country! Connect to Country along a 3.8km trail that is part of the Gateway to the Bundian Way, where ancient stories, ceremony, breathtaking landscapes, and Aboriginal culture come alive. Begin with a traditional smoking ceremony at Jigamy, home to the Keeping Place, before venturing along a section of the Bundian Way to the breathtaking geological feature, the Pinnacles. Traverse serene coastal bushlands that open to sweeping ocean vistas, guided by Country Custodians who share their deep connection to the land. Immerse yourself in the rich knowledge systems of the local Aboriginal community, learning about plants, cultural practices, and the timeless ways of knowing that have sustained this land for thousands of years. This is more than a guided walk; it’s a profound cultural experience. By participating in this cultural tour operated by the Eden Local Aboriginal Land Council, you are helping to make a difference in our local community. Hosting these experiences provides the opportunity for intergenerational knowledge sharing and cultural pride among our people.", "redo_desc_highlights": "Walk the Bundian Way

Incredible Cultural Knowledge
Be guided by a Country Custodian and hear stories of survival, tradition, and deep connection to Country, passed down for thousands of years. Learn about cultural practices, knowledge systems, and the enduring relationship between people and Country.
Diverse and Ancient Landscapes
Walk through ever-changing scenery, from dense native bushland to coastal heath and old water tables exposed by time. Experience the land’s natural beauty and geological history as you journey towards the ocean.
The Pinnacles

{"redo_desc_about": "The Real Sydney Starts Here
Forget the postcards — this isn’t polished Sydney. This is the real story, and it starts in The Rocks. Once a wild colonial outpost built on stolen land, The Rocks was carved out by convicts, ruled by rum, and soaked in scandal. On this 2.5-hour walking tour, you’ll trace the strange and staggering birth of modern Sydney — where the world’s oldest living culture collided with the most outrageous maritime gamble in British history.
Wander crooked lanes and cobbled streets. Hear true stories of escapes, disasters, ghost alleys, and the underground stream still running beneath your feet. Along the way, you’ll sample native bush flavours — like wattle seed tea and Davidson’s plum jam — for a literal taste of the land and its stories.
No boring lectures — just bloody interesting yarns told with heart and humour", "redo_desc_highlights": "- Expert guide — no scripts, just sharp, surprising stories

- True tales of convicts, rebels, escapes, and resistance

{"redo_desc_about": "Discover Wallagoot Lake at Night

Our Night Kayaking Tour is the Sapphire Coast's best kept secret. Discover the magic and adventure of night kayaking on the tranquil and protected Wallagoot lake. Just a short drive from Merimbula (20 minutes) and Tathra (15 minutes), this tour offers a truly unique perspective on the natural world.

We'll begin at the Wallagoot Lake Sailing Club and prepare for our night adventure. As we paddle toward the mouth of the lake, you'll glide through a beautiful wetland area bustling with seabirds like pelicans, black swans, cormorants, and sea eagles. The sandy dunes along the shore are a great spot to see kangaroos as they come out to graze at dusk.

After enjoying sunset, we'll stop for a delicious supper on the shore. You'll feast on a platter featuring local Tilba cheese, crackers, and seasonal fruit, along with a selection of hot drinks and orange juice.

As the sun disappears and the stars begin to emerge, we'll make our way back. This is when the lake truly comes alive. Listen for the chorus of frogs and the rustle of evening birds. Using our special underwater light, we'll search for fish, prawns, jellyfish, and even stingrays in the shallow, protected waters below. With lights on each kayak, we'll paddle safely back together, savouring this surreal and serene experience.

The timing of this tour varies with the seasons, as it's perfectly timed to coincide with the sunset. This makes for a later start in the summer, but a fantastic experience for the entire family.

Supporting Conservation

{"redo_desc_about": "Guba Markay Dance Team are Torres Strait Islanders, the First Nations People of Australia. The third generation carrying forward the stories, dances, and songlines of the seven clan groups of Saibai Island. Each performance reflects our deep connection to culture, identity, and the ongoing preservation of Bamaga traditions within the Northern Peninsula Area. Please note: this is a family and alcohol-free event.", "redo_desc_highlights": "Guba Markay was established in 1990. It is a proud Bamaga Traditional Dance Group, showcasing the movement, history, and cultural legacy of people who relocated from Saibai Island in the Torres Strait to Muttee Head, mainland Australia in 1947. Through our performances we honour the strength and resilience of our Elders and ancestors.

Our achievements include the Gold Winners 2020 Sydney Dance Rites, Gold Laura Festival 2018, Gold Weipa Cultural Festival 1995 and many more. We perform at festivals and deliver a full cultural experience showcasing our seven clan stories and ancestral movements.", "redo_desc_what_included": "Visitors will be introduced to the Kala Lagaw Ya language, one of the traditional languages of the Torres Strait, through guided storytelling sessions. These stories share knowledge of the Tagai constellation, seasonal changes, island life, and cultural values passed down through generations. This creates a meaningful opportunity for visitors to not just observe, but understand the worldview and knowledge systems of Torres Strait Islander people.

The experience is further enriched through traditional island food tasting, where guests can sample local foods such as fresh seafood, damper, coconut-based dishes, and other culturally significant ingredients. These tastings highlight the strong relationship between people, sea country, and sustainable practices.
